decision.trend: Research has been focused on developing high-entropy alloys with excellent wear resistance and surface protection properties. Various processing techniques such as mechanical alloying, spark plasma sintering, and selective laser melting have been explored to improve the microstructure and properties of these alloys. The use of refractory high-entropy alloys has shown promising results in terms of high-temperature stability and resistance to radiation damage.
decision.unsolved: The adhesion of high-entropy alloys to a Cu matrix remains a challenge, and further research is needed to develop a suitable material that can adhere to the Cu surface while maintaining excellent wear resistance and surface protection properties.
decision.lever: nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy film deposition
decision.why: The deposition of a nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy film on the Cu surface could potentially improve the adhesion and wear resistance of the alloy. This approach has shown promising results in previous studies, and further research is needed to optimize the film deposition process and properties.
